title: Contributing to other projects
description: Etiquette for opening issues and pull requests in a repository you do not own.

rules.title: Check for duplicates
rules.text: Before starting, look for an existing issue or open PR for the same change. Do not open a competing one without agreement.

rules.title: Keep the PR template
rules.text: Use the repository PR template and keep every section and checkbox, including the ones left unchecked.

rules.title: Read the contributing guide
rules.text: Read CONTRIBUTING and any AI contribution policy before opening an issue or PR, and follow the target branch it names.

rules.title: Link and discuss first
rules.text: Link a PR to the issue it resolves, and discuss non-trivial features in an issue before implementing them.

rules.title: Keep it focused
rules.text: Keep PRs small and focused. Do not bundle unrelated cleanups into a feature PR.

rules.title: No busywork PRs
rules.text: Skip one-off PRs for a single typo or an isolated style tweak unless maintainers asked for them.

rules.title: Labels and changelog
rules.text: Pick labels and the changelog entry deliberately. Check which labels include or exclude a change from the release notes.

rules.title: Split frontend and backend
rules.text: Send frontend and backend changes as separate PRs when they deploy on different schedules. Land the backend first when the frontend depends on it.

rules.title: Report test runs
rules.text: State in the PR which test commands you ran and what they returned.

rules.title: Backport conventions
rules.text: Mark backport PRs the way the project requires, for example a branch prefix in the title, and target the maintenance branch.

rules.title: Respond to review
rules.text: Address review comments in follow-up work and say what changed in the reply.
